title: The Farmer and the Viper
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: One winter a Farmer found a Viper frozen and numb with cold, and out of pity picked it up and placed it in his bosom. The Viper was no sooner revived by the warmth than it turned upon its benefactor and inflicted a fatal bite upon him; and as the poor man lay dying, he cried, "I have only got what I deserved, for taking compassion on so villainous a creature." Kindness is thrown away upon the evil.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, in what season did the Farmer find the Viper?
options: Spring
Summer
Winter
Autumn

questions.prompt: According to the passage, in what condition was the Viper when the Farmer found it?
options: Angry and hissing
Injured by a hawk
Hiding under a rock
Frozen and numb with cold

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Farmer do out of pity?
options: Picked it up and placed it in his bosom
Left it to warm itself in the sun
Carried it to a nearby fire
Wrapped it in a blanket by the door

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Viper do once it was revived by the warmth?
options: Slithered quietly away
Turned upon its benefactor and inflicted a fatal bite
Thanked the Farmer with a hiss
Fell back asleep in his bosom

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "benefactor" mean in "turned upon its benefactor"?
options: A person who does good or provides help to another
A person who harms another
A person who studies snakes
A stranger passing by

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "villainous" mean in "so villainous a creature"?
options: Extremely small
Beautiful in appearance
Wicked or evil
Harmless and gentle

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Farmer say he "only got what he deserved"?
options: He thinks he should have killed the Viper as soon as he found it
He believes he should have known better than to show compassion to a creature of an evil, dangerous nature
He blames the cold weather for the whole incident
He believes vipers are always harmless unless provoked

questions.prompt: Which statement, made explicit at the end of the passage, best captures the point of the fable?
options: Winter is the most dangerous season for farmers
Vipers cannot survive extreme cold
One should always help creatures in distress
Kindness is thrown away upon the evil

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what are the Farmer's exact dying words?
options: "Someone please save me from this creature!"
"I never should have gone out in the snow"
"Tell my family I love them"
"I have only got what I deserved, for taking compassion on so villainous a creature"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what ultimately revived the Viper?
options: A drink of water
The heat of a nearby fire
The warmth of the Farmer's body
Sunlight

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of bite did the Viper inflict on the Farmer?
options: A fatal bite
A minor, harmless bite
A bite that only frightened him
No bite at all, only a hiss

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "compassion" mean in "taking compassion on so villainous a creature"?
options: Suspicion or distrust
Fear or dread
Curiosity about something unfamiliar
Sympathy that moves one to help

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Viper's attack suggest about trying to change a dangerous creature's nature through kindness?
options: Kindness always transforms even the most dangerous creatures
A creature's harmful nature may not change no matter how it is treated
The Viper only attacked because it was still cold
The Farmer's kindness went completely unnoticed by the Viper

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Farmer kills a Viper he finds frozen in the snow
A Viper warms a freezing Farmer and saves his life
A Farmer warms a frozen Viper out of pity, and the Viper repays him with a fatal bite once revived
A Farmer and a Viper become lasting companions
